faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Tavares?
faqs.a: Tavares pricing follows the lakefront pattern: roof, boathouse, and dock gaps inspected and quoted as one waterfront job in writing, with in-town homes priced as the simpler seals they usually are.

faqs.q: Bats are in our Tavares lake house — can you exclude them this spring?
faqs.a: Spring timing decides everything. If we are before April 15, yes — exclusion is legal through that date. From April 16 to August 14, Florida prohibits excluding or blocking bats because pups are flightless in the roost; spring and summer work becomes inspection, species identification — Brazilian free-tailed and evening bats are the lake country's house bats — sealing of unused openings, and a booked exclusion for late August. Anyone offering to seal a colony in May is offering an illegal job.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Clermont?
faqs.a: Clermont quotes split between new-build gap packages — priced by roofline after inspection — and lakefront or historic work, each written separately. Tortoise identification on a lot is part of the inspection conversation, never a removal line item.

faqs.q: Our new Clermont subdivision has tortoise burrows everywhere — what does that mean for our yard?
faqs.a: It means your yard came with a protected tenant. Gopher tortoises are State Threatened; their burrows cannot be filled, blocked, or disturbed without an FWC permit, and construction within 25 feet requires one. In practice, most Clermont homeowners coexist easily: fence with a gap strategy that keeps dogs from the burrow, mow around the apron, enjoy the tenant. If a burrow conflicts with a pool or addition, the path is an FWC permit and an Authorized Agent — a process we explain, but not a service we sell.

Clermont's growth edge is tortoise edge — new phases meet burrows constantly, and our residential role is identification and buffer guidance for homeowners whose yards inherit a protected neighbor. For the houses themselves, the inspection emphasizes ridge-country details: two-story rooflines, chimney chases on the newer builds, and the oak bridges of old downtown. Call (844) 544-3498 from the hills or the lakes; the approach differs by slope, and we know both.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Leesburg?
faqs.a: Leesburg pricing follows the waterfront-versus-in-town divide: canal homes carry dock and boathouse items, in-town homes carry canopy and fascia items, each inspected and written as its own figure.

faqs.q: How large does a Leesburg canal alligator have to be before FWC acts?
faqs.a: The program's working threshold is four feet and a threat: an alligator four feet or longer that poses a danger to people, pets, or property is what FWC's nuisance alligator program sends its contracted trappers for. Smaller gators in a Leesburg canal are generally tolerated residents. Keep dogs leashed and away from the bank at dawn and dusk — most incidents happen there — never feed or approach one, and report a large or bold animal to FWC. No private company may book gator removal, including us.

faqs.q: Our Mount Dora inn has bats — how do you handle a business property?
faqs.a: Quietly and in season. We survey at dusk to count exits and identify the colony — free-tailed or evening bats in most Lake County buildings — then, inside the August 15 to April 15 legal window, fit one-way devices, confirm the roost is empty, seal, and clean guano with proper precautions. Outside the window we inspect and prepare so the legal-season job takes days, not weeks. All of it is scheduled around your guests; a historic inn's bats are a facilities problem, and we treat them with a facilities mindset.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Eustis?
faqs.a: Eustis pricing is direction-based: lakefront scope and forest-acreage scope are different inspections, quoted separately in writing so a lake cottage never pays for a barn it does not have.

faqs.q: A bear raided trash on our forest-edge Eustis street — what now?
faqs.a: Secure the food and the bear usually self-resolves. Black bears are excluded from Florida's nuisance-take rule — no private removal exists — and FWC's bear program manages repeat animals. Use bear-resistant cans or keep trash in the garage until pickup morning, bring in pet food and bird seed during active weeks, and clean grills. Most east Eustis bear visits are a young male passing through the forest edge in spring or fall; a neighborhood that removes attractants together sees him move on.

faqs.q: How much does wildlife removal cost in Lady Lake?
faqs.a: Lady Lake figures are yard-and-home combined where they should be: a mole program, a skirt replacement, and an attic seal are separate written lines after one inspection, so retirement budgets can choose sequencing without pressure.

faqs.q: What is tunneling in my Lady Lake yard — mole or gopher?
faqs.a: Run a finger along the damage. Eastern moles push up raised surface tunnels — soft ridges you can press flat — and small cone-shaped hills where they dig deep. Southeastern pocket gophers, present in this sandy country, shove up larger fan-shaped sand mounds with the entrance plugged at the side, and they eat roots and bulbs from below, which moles, hunting worms and grubs, do not. The treatments differ, so we confirm on inspection before quoting either program.

Retirement living shapes the wildlife work: single-story homes, lanais and birdcages, golf-cart paths, and residents who spend real time in their yards — which means armadillo digging, mole tunnels, and pond Muscovy ducks get noticed and reported with precision. Raccoons work the older mobile-home communities' crawl spaces, and squirrels work the oaks.

Lady Lake gets detail-oriented service: yard-level diagnosis (mole ridge versus pocket gopher fan versus armadillo cone-hole) done carefully, because here the yard is the living room. Mobile and manufactured homes get skirt inspections, since most of their animal problems live underneath. Pond associations get the Muscovy talk straight — Control Order rules, no relocation, feeding is the root — delivered kindly but without varnish.
